products.what: PPTX Player SDK is a client-side JavaScript engine that renders PowerPoint .pptx decks to HTML and SVG and plays them click by click: entrance, exit and emphasis effects, morph transitions and embedded media. It runs offline in any modern browser or WebView, with no server conversion and no Office install. Full source included.
quickstart: press → or Space to step through the deck
compare: $14 one-time; plays offline in the browser or a WKWebView
faq: Can I play a PowerPoint file in the browser with its animations?
Yes. The engine renders each slide to HTML/SVG and steps through the click sequence: entrance, exit and emphasis effects, morph transitions and media.
Does it need a server or Microsoft Office?
No. Everything runs client-side. Serve the player folder from any static web server and open it in a browser.
Does it work offline or inside a native app?
Yes. It runs offline, and on iOS, iPadOS and macOS you can load the same folder in a WKWebView. Android and Electron WebViews work the same way.
What happens with a slide whose XML is broken?
The engine repairs stray & characters and plays the slide normally. If the XML is still broken, it renders what it can and reports an error instead of dropping the slide silently.
Is it a subscription?
No. One-time purchase, full source included.

products.name: Scan-to-Grade: Scanned Exams to Excel (Python)
products.title: Scan-to-Grade: Scanned Exams to Excel (Python)
products.description: Cropper + OMR grader together: drop in a scanner batch, get an Excel gradebook. Runs offline; student data never leaves your PC. One-time, source.
products.summary: QR Cropper and OMR Auto-Grader together: a scanned batch in, an Excel gradebook out.
products.what: Scan-to-Grade is a Python package that turns a batch of scanned answer sheets into an Excel gradebook. It reads the QR on each page, pairs fronts and backs, deskews and crops every answer cell, grades bubbles, multi-answer marks, O/X parts and ordering bubbles, and writes scores, item analysis and a re-check list. It runs offline.
compare: Bubble grading; you build the scan-to-Excel pipeline
$79 one-time; QR page sorting, cropping, grading and Excel export in one
faq: Can I turn scanned paper tests into an Excel gradebook automatically?
Yes. Drop the scanner batch in a folder and run it. You get gradebook.xlsx with scores, item analysis and a re-check list, plus results.json and recheck.csv.
Does student data leave my computer?
No. It runs offline on Windows, macOS or Linux. Nothing is uploaded.
Can the pages be scanned in any order or rotation?
Yes. Each page carries a QR, so mixed batches, back sides and 90/180/270-degree turns are sorted out automatically.
Does it grade handwriting or essays?
No. Short answers, essays and handwriting stay with the teacher, who sees the cropped cell images.
What do I need to run it?
Python 3.10+, opencv-python-headless, numpy and openpyxl. One-time purchase, full source included.

It fills in only grades it is confident about, never overwrites a mark a teacher already made, and sends the rest to a re-check list. Runnable demo exports to Excel.

faq: Which mark types can it read?
Single and multi-answer bubbles, circled words, O/X boxes and ordering bubbles.
Will it overwrite grades a teacher already entered?
No. It fills only confident grades, keeps existing teacher marks and lists any disagreement for re-checking.
Is there an open-source alternative?
Yes, for example OMRChecker (MIT) for bubble sheets. This engine adds O/X, circled-word and ordering items and the confident-only grading rule.
Does it work with my scanner?
It works on scanned images from any scanner. Pair it with the QR Cropper, or get both in the Scan-to-Grade Bundle.
Is it a subscription?
No. One-time purchase, full source included.

products.what: QR-Anchored Answer Sheet Cropper is a Python and OpenCV tool for scanned exams. Print a small QR on each sheet and drop in a mixed scanner batch. It identifies each page by its QR, pairs fronts and backs, corrects rotation and skew, and crops every answer cell into a clean, aligned image at about 200 dpi. It runs offline.
compare: QR-anchored perspective warp; you write the rest
$39 one-time; batch sorting, front/back pairing and cell cropping
faq: How do I crop answer regions from scanned exam sheets with a QR code?
Print the QR payload on each sheet, scan the batch and run the cropper. It reads the QR in the page corners, warps each answer table to a millimetre grid and cuts every cell.
Can I sort a mixed scanner batch by student?
Yes. Pages are grouped into front/back pairs per student from their QR codes. Pages from another exam are reported as stray.
Does rotation or skew matter?
No. It handles skew and 90/180/270-degree turns.
What scan resolution do I need?
150 dpi or higher. The demo uses 200 dpi.
What do I need to run it?
Python 3.10+, opencv-python-headless and numpy on Windows, macOS or Linux. One-time purchase, full source included.

products.name: Context-Gated Voice Commands – Offline
products.title: Context-Gated Voice Commands – Offline
products.description: Rust engine that tracks the current situation second by second and runs only the voice commands that fit it, ignoring background talk. Offline.
products.summary: A Rust library and CLI that infers the current situation from audio features and lets through only the voice commands that fit it.
products.what: Context-Gated Voice Commands is a Rust library and CLI that estimates which phase a scene is in (a lesson, a meeting, a shop floor) from acoustic features and cues, second by second, and decides whether each voice command may run, needs a wake word, or is blocked. It runs offline and ships with classroom, meeting and retail presets plus a seeded simulator.
compare: Fixed command grammars, no situation model
$29 one-time; gates commands by the detected phase, offline
faq: How do I reduce false voice command triggers in a noisy room?
Gate commands by context. The engine tracks which phase is active and, per phase, allows a command, requires a wake word or blocks it.
How does it detect the situation?

A probabilistic filter over phases with configured transitions and acoustic profiles (voice count, loudness, overlap, main-speaker share, media playing), plus optional spoken or app cues, updated once per second.
Can I model my own situations?

Yes. Define phases, durations, transitions, acoustic profiles and command rules in a TOML file, validate it with scene-engine validate, and simulate it. Classroom, meeting and retail-store presets are built in.
How do I use it in my app?
Add it as a Rust path dependency, feed one observation per second to SceneFilter and call gate::decide for each command. The CLI can also stream JSONL observations in and phase snapshots out.
Does it need the cloud or Python?
No. It runs locally with Rust 1.85 or newer, with no account, API key or Python. One-time purchase, full source included.

products.what: ShapeFit adds the hold-to-shape gesture from Apple Notes and GoodNotes to your own drawing app. When the user pauses at the end of a stroke, it snaps to a clean line, circle, ellipse, rectangle, triangle or polygon, and leaves scribbles alone. Pure geometry, no ML model, zero dependencies: a Rust crate plus a drop-in Swift file with identical results.
compare: Swift SDK with an ML model
Rust crate + Swift file, source included
$9 one-time; no ML, no MAU limits, identical Rust and Swift output
faq: How do I add Apple Notes-style hold-to-shape to my app?
Feed the stroke points to ShapeFit when the pen pauses. It returns a clean shape, or leaves the stroke alone if it is a scribble.
Does it work with PencilKit?
Yes. The Swift file works with PencilKit or any canvas.
Which shapes does it recognise?
Lines with 45° snap, circles and ellipses, upright rectangles, triangles and polygons up to 6 corners.
Does it use machine learning?
No. It is pure geometry with zero dependencies and no training data. The Rust and Swift versions give identical results, checked on 600 strokes.
Is it a subscription?
No. One-time purchase, full source included.
